title: Zariski's Main Theorem for a monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R[X]$ an ideal of the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $S=R[X]/I$, an $R$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal such that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], and let $S'\subseteq S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then there is $g\in S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the map $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, of localizations at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] induced by the inclusion $S'\subseteq S$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, line 30735; its proof uses Lemma 00PQ)
